title: Germany: Friedrich Merz fights for survival after election defeats
summary: Pressure is mounting on Chancellor Friedrich Merz after his CDU's defeats in two state elections, which saw more gains for the far-right AfD. Follow DW.
byline: Dmytro Hubenko, Darko Janjevic, Richard Connor, Kieran Burke, Roshni Majumdar

image.caption: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the two state election outcomes 'a disaster'Image: Christian Mang/REUTERS

blocks.text: Merz's political future at risk after double election defeat

Chancellor Friedrich Merz struck a defiant tone on Sunday night, insisting that he is still the right person to lead his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Germany despite his party's losses in the two state elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, vowing to push on with the reforms his government has promised.

But that defiance is unlikely to ease the intense pressure on Merz, who was already on the back foot heading into the polls amid low approval ratings and a surging far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD).

The CDU leadership is meeting on Monday morning to discuss how the party can recover from that devastating double blow, which saw the center-right party fail to reach the 5% threshold needed to enter parliament in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
We will bring you the fallout from that, and whether Merz still has the backing of his party.
We will also be bringing you reactions from the AfD and Social Democrats, who will be holding their own press conferences later on Monday.
